CoverMap v0.7.2 · August 2026 · FEASIBILITY DEMONSTRATOR · IML 2 · four countries · not clinical guidance

CoverMap — matching antivenom to the snakes that actually bite

Antivenom is species-specific: the wrong product does not save the patient. CoverMap joins what bites where to what each product is actually proven to neutralise to who can reach care — and turns it into a costed, named plan a procurement programme can act on. Demonstrated on four countries covering three different failure regimes.

The problem is a decision, not a discovery. When rural Ghana substituted an unsuitable antivenom against the carpet viper, district case-fatality rose 1.8% → 12.1% (Visser 2008). The people who buy and place antivenom must choose which product and where — with no tool that joins species range to evidence-graded product coverage to access. CoverMap is that tool.

One method, three regimes. In West Africa the binding gap is which product is stocked and where (several products, wildly different Echis cover). In India a single southern-sourced polyvalent is used nationwide, so the gap is regional venom variation and non-Big-Four species. In Kenya the failing products were withdrawn in 2022 after national QC testing, so the gap is availability and placement. The same engine expresses all three — the strongest evidence that it generalises.

Four demonstrators, one engine

GHANA · PLACEMENT

86.0%
of the carpet-viper burden brought within reach of a species-appropriate antivenom, via 25 hospitals (from ~0% under a failing product)
  • 4,654 vials/yr demand forecast (~$371,114)
  • 5.6% of burden beyond ANY hospital — structural gap, shown
  • 24/25 hospitals stay chosen under a flattened gradient

36.8%
of India's snakebite burden sits where the standard ASV likely underperforms — ~20,484 deaths/yr inside that gap. An ordinal model output, not a measurement: no published national figure exists.
  • Burden anchored to the Million Death Study (~58,000/yr)
  • Mortality weighted 94% rural, per the MDS's own finding
  • 3,575 hospital-tier facilities; only 0.6% of burden >50 km from one

86.6%
of expected snakebite attendances within reach via 45 of 401 hospital-tier facilities — the failing products were withdrawn (2022 QC); the open question is where adequate stock sits
  • 1,569 vials/yr demand forecast (~$125,520)
  • County populations pinned to the KNBS 2019 census, exactly
  • 42/45 hospitals stay chosen with the unconfirmed highlands rate halved
Anchor: implied 8.7/100k national attendances, inside Coombs 1997's multi-area 13.8/100k

How it works

  1. Species → district. Which medically important snakes occur where, at eco-zone resolution.
  2. The novel core: an evidence-graded coverage matrix. Which product is actually proven to neutralise which species, graded A (WHO risk-benefit-assessed) · B (peer-reviewed preclinical) · C (manufacturer claim) · ~ (partial/paraspecific) · ✗ (published evidence AGAINST neutralisation) · – (no activity claimed) · · (no data). Two rules are enforced in code: a manufacturer label is never promoted to "covered", and published evidence of failure overrides every higher grade. Comparable evidence exists as literature; what did not is this cross-tabulation in machine-readable form, keyed to placement.
  3. Access. Real facility coordinates and distance to care, so coverage means reachable coverage.
  4. Burden, anchored. Population × published incidence/mortality — every country checked against a published national figure before anything else is computed.
  5. The decision. A greedy maximal-coverage optimiser returns a named, priority-ordered, costed pre-positioning plan: which hospital, how many vials, what it costs — the demand forecast a stockpile programme needs.

Honest by design — the guardrails, stated up front

We headline coverage, not deaths. Coverage (% of burden within reach of an appropriate product) is what the tool actually controls. Mortality is reported as a bounded decision-gap versus a worst case (an ineffective product everywhere) — explicitly not "extra lives saved versus today", since effective antivenom already reaches some patients. In West Africa it is anchored to a directly observed measurement (case-fatality 1.8% → 12.1% when an ineffective product was substituted in rural Ghana, Visser 2008) rather than a synthetic chain of assumed parameters.
We work in the facility frame, and say so. The published incidence figures are hospital attendance rates — patients who already reached care. Outputs are therefore antivenom demand at facilities, not total community burden (which runs ~10× higher). An earlier version treated attendance as community incidence and then applied a care-seeking multiplier — a double discount that understated the vial forecast by roughly half. That is corrected; care-seeking is no longer applied anywhere.
We publish what is not sourced. A parameter provenance audit ships with the code (audit_parameters.py): of the load-bearing numbers, it labels each CITED, DERIVED or ASSUMED, and names the three largest exposures — India's ordinal adequacy tiers, Nigeria's constructed zone rates (no published per-zone figure exists), and Ghana's coastal rate (no published figure of any kind). Verification scripts check arithmetic; this audit checks provenance, because the two are different questions.
No impact figure may exceed total national mortality. This is enforced in code, not promised in prose: Nigeria's upper bound is capped at the highest published national estimate (2,640, GBD 2019 UI upper) and the cap is disclosed wherever it binds. India's coverage-gap is a strict subset of MDS mortality, never an addition to it.
Artifacts are disclosed and quantified, not hidden. Urban units inherit their zone's rural incidence, which overstates city burden. In Nigeria we show the consequence and prove it doesn't drive the plan (only 1.2% of vials go to the FCT or Lagos). In India we fixed it at the source, weighting mortality 94% rural per the Million Death Study.
Stock is unobservable subnationally — so CoverMap models placement choices, never a false inventory. Access is straight-line ≤50 km, a documented proxy for travel time. Coverage rests largely on preincubation ED50/antivenomics, not clinical trials — grade B is not proven bedside efficacy. Not clinical guidance.

Verification record — 285 checks, six suites

Every number in every artifact is re-derived from raw inputs by an independent script that fails loudly on any mismatch. All four pipelines reproduce from data committed in the repository — no network, no temporary files.

SuiteChecksResultCovers
verify_ghana.py54PASSpopulation vs census, burden re-derivation, optimiser, demand arithmetic, mortality ceiling, artifact consistency, citations
verify_nigeria.py62PASSreproducibility, scaled population (guards the 550k regression), rates declared a construction, death ceiling, the flagged mortality-gap tension, urban artifact
verify_india.py73PASSstate rates locked to the published MDS table verbatim, exact state populations, 94/6 rural weighting, ordinal-tier disclosure, published sub-national anchors carried
verify_kenya.py29PASScounty populations pinned to the KNBS 2019 census, frame guard (no care-seeking multiplier), market-availability product rule, cut-rule bilateral check, per-hospital reassignment from raw geometry
verify_crosscountry.py67PASSshared parameters identical, honesty invariants hold everywhere, no stale or contradictory numbers
verify_figures.py13 figsPASSOCRs every shipped figure and requires every percentage displayed to be a value the model actually produced — text checks cannot see a number baked into a PNG

Who it is for

The WHO Antivenom Stockpile Programme and national NTD programmes — the actors whose remit is exactly "which product, how much, where". The output is deliberately the thing they already have to produce: a costed pre-positioning plan with a demand forecast.

CoverMap v0.7.2 · August 2026 — v0.7.2 — the front page catches up with the project, no number moves. The index's verification table still listed four suites with pre-Kenya counts (India 62, cross-country 34) and its 'four demonstrators' grid showed three countries — while the README beside it said six suites and 285 checks. Both now match the shipped reality (285 checks + a 13-figure OCR pass; Kenya card added). Adds a four-map overview so the plan is visible at a glance. Also ships the two Kenya brief figures the v0.7.0 upload omitted — kenya.html had displayed broken images in production. Same lesson as v0.7.1, one door further in: checks prove arithmetic, not that the published page shows it. v0.7.1 — documentation-only correction, no number moves. The README's reproduce-it-yourself block listed four verification suites when there are five: verify_kenya.py was missing, so anyone following the README ran 256 of the 285 checks and never touched Kenya. It also said 11 shipped figures when the OCR suite covers 13. The methods page's Current figures line still listed three countries. And every page was date-stamped July 2026 while carrying an August build. None of this changes a result; all of it breaks the one promise the project actually makes, which is that a stranger can re-derive the numbers without asking us anything. Logged rather than quietly overwritten. v0.7.0 — adds KENYA, the fourth demonstrator and third failure regime (availability and placement: the failing products were withdrawn in 2022 after national QC testing). Built against a provenance sheet written before the code; county populations pinned to the KNBS 2019 census; product rule enforces market availability. Three review rounds: a self-caught coarseness rejection, a FAILED independent adversarial review (two critical errors - a population-distribution artifact and a treated fraction contradicting its source - both corrected), and a passing re-review with all numbers reproduced end-to-end independently. v0.6.2 — separates DEMONSTRATED FAILURE from ABSENCE OF DATA in the coverage matrix. PANAF-Premium x Naja katiensis was rendering as partial cover while its own cell recorded a measured failure (Khochare 2024, 11.16 LD50/mL, below the 20 threshold); four untested Atractaspis cells were rendering in the same red as documented failures, asserting more than the evidence supports. Failure now overrides every higher grade and is visually distinct from no-claim and no-data. Also corrects six stale figures in the methods page and adds publish.py, which diffs generated output against the published site instead of copying by hand. v0.6.1 — corrects three Ghana figure titles that still displayed 87.5%, the pre-v0.4 coverage value, while every text KPI on the same page said 86.0%; the numbers are now read from the model JSON and a fifth verification suite OCRs every shipped figure to keep image and text in agreement. v0.6 added the targeting-scenario table for India and a parameter-provenance table to all three briefs. v0.5 confirmed 4 of 10 assumed parameters against primary sources and labelled the remaining 6 NOT CONFIRMED. v0.4 corrected the care-seeking double discount and India's state death rates.
